subject: Filling only one part of a histogram.

messages.author: a1331fc093f52833
messages.subject: Filling only one part of a histogram.
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to fill in, only one part of a histogram.
plo <- ggplot(as.data.frame(rnorm(1000)),aes(x=rnorm(1000))) +
geom_histogram() + geom_vline(xintercept=0); plo

How do you the part of the histogram, which is right of the vline?

Thanks for your help,
Cedric

messages.author: 70ab9fabb9f066d8
messages.subject: Re: Filling only one part of a histogram.
parts:
With a little rewrite of your example, like this:

ggplot(data.frame(x = rnorm(1000)), aes(x = x)) +
geom_histogram(aes(fill = x < 0 )) + geom_vline(xintercept=0) +
scale_fill_manual(values = c("black","grey20"))

Charlotte

messages.author: a1331fc093f52833
messages.subject: Re: Filling only one part of a histogram.
parts:
Dear Charlotte,

Thank you so much for your help. That's very much appreciated.
Although your solution works well for some example, it doesn't seem to
be robust enough for different choices of cut-off points. Check this
example for instance:

x= rnorm(1000)
ggplot(data.frame(x), aes(x = x)) +
geom_histogram(aes(fill = x < 1 )) + geom_vline(xintercept=1) +
scale_fill_manual(values = c("red4","blue4"))

In general, the coloured part of the histogram will not exactly follow
the vertical line at 1.0. This is, I think because we are producing
two different histograms, as opposed to colouring one part of a single
histogram. With the standard plotting devices, you can do this with
the polygon function:

Rvec <- rnorm(1000); cutoff <- 1.5
h <- hist(Rvec,plot=FALSE,breaks=70)
y <- smooth(smooth(h$density)); x <- h$mids
plot(x,y, type="l",xlab=expression(r[ij]),ylab="Density");
grid(5,5,lwd=2)
polygon(c(cutoff, x[x>=cutoff]), c(0, y[x>=cutoff]), density=20)

I wonder whether the use of geom_polygon would solve the problem. What
do you think?
Best wishes,
Cedric
